summary: Most of D.2's scheduler is legitimate scheduler-layer mechanism (the DIRECT worklist, lanes, Mattern's detector, the replay monitor), but §9 dresses it as cells and propagators that no phase allocates, and that dressing hides three detector-input defects an exhaustive model check finds: the idle mark cannot record re-activation, cross-executor notifications are missing, and per-run state sits in process-wide singletons. The measurements matter more than the vocabulary: in the three files holding 88 % of the census's fires, 84-89 % of fires have the single attribute-map cell as first output, so D.2's home rule puts them on one executor. That cell's :type facet composes type-unify-or-top, so the per-cell fence also covers those fires, and D.2's own D2P-5 rule already points to whole-network K=1. The fence is a gating decision, not the monotone map D.2 calls it, and the alternation adds one CALM coordination per fenced wave, so the detector is not 'the only non-monotone act'. The replay monitor as specified is blind to lost updates and cannot separate fence contamination from bugs, and 'K = 1 is the same code' is contradicted by §6.6 vs §6.7. The per-component classification (legitimate scheduler layer vs step-think) is in component_classification.
strongest_point_in_favour: The order of the work. P0.5 and P1 establish the asynchronous-iteration hypotheses (join merges from combinators, monotone fires, no in-fire topology) before any executor runs in parallel, so the K>1 scheduler is only asked to be fast, never to be careful. D.2 also gets the layering right where it matters most. The fence is a scheduler response to a declared cell property and is never decided by reading code. BSP is kept as the Kleene-iterate reference dynamics, which turns the old scheduler into a co-inductive oracle instead of a fallback. The epoch counters remove D.1's two resets honestly. On the fence itself, which I attack hardest: it does keep K>1 correct when non-join cells are present without relying on care, it is labelled scaffolding with a measured exit criterion (the fenced set in every epoch record), and D.2 already wrote down the simpler alternative (D2P-5) together with the rule that chooses between them. My measurements apply that rule; they do not overturn the reasoning behind it.
component_classification: s0-fire: a genuine propagator (reads cells, writes joins). On-network.

owner-drain: scheduler realization of a write to a cell another executor owns. Legitimate at the scheduler layer, but modelling it as a propagator over an ever-growing Set lane hides the consumer cursor, which is exactly cons_i.

quiescence-detector: a legitimate scheduler algorithm (the CALM coordination), mislabelled as a propagator. 'stable-twice' is memory across fires (it breaks statelessness, DESIGN_PRINCIPLES.org:700). Two scans are needed only because the K slot groups are not one cell, since a cell read is atomic. Its output, boundary-epoch, is the one input that deserves to be a real cell.

S0 <-> S0-fenced alternation: imposed ordering that changes semantics (it decides the order in which non-join merges see their writes). By DESIGN_PRINCIPLES.org:884-890 that puts it at the wrong layer. It is scaffolding for a cell-layer defect, which D.2 §12.1 already concedes.
replay monitor: a test-time instrument; being off-network is legitimate.
epoch records / exec-changed: the scheduler emits data at boundaries, which is legitimate. exec-changed is scratch, not a cell.
E verdict: on-network in intent (SRE property cells). The fence-as-bridge is a non-monotone gate dressed as a monotone map.
lanes: scheduler realization of cell writes; legitimate.
assignment: write-once per epoch at the topology stratum, so a sound cell, but it belongs to the run, not the process.
scheduler-k: configuration, not information. A max-lattice cell is the wrong model.
P1b dispositions: mostly on-network rewrites. 'declared stratum' for choosing bridges is sound. 2 of the 8 absence-reading sites have no fitting disposition.

P2 K=1 executor: chaotic iteration over a worklist, legitimate at the scheduler layer. P3 executor: legitimate, but the home rule and cell granularity impose sequentiality that the propagator structure does not.

findings.claim_attacked: "a fire runs on the executor that owns its first output" (§5), "a fire's home is the owner of its first declared output … Measured adequate: ≤ 10 % foreign writes (P0 Q4)" (§6.7)
findings.evidence:
MEASUREMENT. Command: timeout -k 10 400 "/Applications/Racket v9.3/bin/racket" /Users/avanti/.hermes/profiles/logos-language-designer/cache/scratch/d3/C3/home_fence_probe.rkt <worktree>/racket/prologos/benchmarks/comparative/{constraints-adversarial,type-adversarial,implicit-args}.prologos (BSP observer at HEAD ae27532f, racket/ = main c1f389ab). Home is computed with D.2's rule: owner of the first output, round-robin, K=8.
- constraints-adversarial: 1142 fires; executor 1 gets 1020 (89.3 %); 1010 have first output cell 49, attribute-map-merge-fn.
- type-adversarial: 1112 fires; executor 1 gets 942 (84.7 %).
- implicit-args: 150 fires; executor 1 gets 130 (86.7 %).
- Calibration: the fire totals equal P0's census (comparative-census-bsp.jsonl rr.fires = 1142, 1112, 150). These three files hold 2404 of that census's 2745 fires.
- Power: the same instrument spreads the other 334 fires over the 7 remaining executors, so it can report a spread.
The attribute map is one cell per typing network: a two-level pointwise hash, typing-propagators.rkt:447. P0's 'hub cell, degree 1247' is that cell. hub_identity_probe.rkt on constraints-adversarial finds, in the largest snapshot (657 propagators, as in P0's census), the degree-1247 cell is id 49 with merge attribute-map-merge-fn, and it is the FIRST output of 595 of the 657 propagators. The ≤ 10 % foreign-write figure is therefore a symptom: nearly every fire is homed together. Any other home rule sends 86 % of fires' writes as deltas to the hub's owner, whose joins of the whole hash serialize; the P0 §2.2 corpus merge time is 27.4 of 87.6 ms. Either way one executor carries most of S0. The §2 item 3 models (H-S + K=8 at 4.07× / 3.26×, from s0-par = fire/min(n,K) in p0-profile.rkt:122-123) assume a K-way split within each round that this rule cannot produce.
findings.direction: Let ownership follow the lattice's declared product structure rather than the cell id. attribute-map-merge-fn is pointwise per position and per facet, so with P1a's join:pointwise combinator the cell declares itself a product. Each (cell, position) key then has an owner, a delta is a per-position record, and a fire's home is the owner of the position it writes. The alternative is for PPN 4C to give each position its own cell. Restate §2 item 3's models with the home rule applied: the observer already gives per-executor fire time. Add 'max-executor share of fire time' to P0-8 and to P3's entry gate.
findings.falsifier: A run of the heavy files under D.2's rule, at K = 8, with max-home share ≤ ~1/K + 0.1. Or D.2 adopting a home rule or a cell decomposition that spreads the attribute map's writers with no single-owner join bottleneck.

findings.section: D.2 §6.3 The fence and the D2P-5 decision rule; §5 'the stratum boundary is the only barrier'; §8 alternation row; §2 item 3 'P0 never measured that share'
findings.claim_attacked: "at K > 1 every propagator with a fenced output runs in a deterministic BSP sub-run after the DIRECT run quiesces, and the two alternate until neither has work" together with "the stratum boundary is the only barrier" and "the realizable K>1 share … P0 never measured that share"
findings.evidence:
MEASUREMENT and THEOREM.
(1) The type merge is inside the hub cell: facet-merge :type → merge-classify-inhabit (typing-propagators.rkt:401-406) → type-unify-or-top (classify-inhabit.rkt:171). The attribute map's installed merge therefore carries F3(b), which stays open until O-12 (ii). The fence is kept per cell (§6.3), so the attribute-map cell is fenced.
(2) Same probe as C3-1. Fires with an attribute-map output: 1010/1142 (88.4 %), 930/1112 (83.6 %), 130/150 (86.7 %). Rounds containing a fenced fire: 203/212, 157/182, 29/29. Fenced/unfenced phase switches in BSP round order, a proxy for alternations: 82 over 31 runs, 69 over 37 runs, 12 over 5 runs. P0 §2.3 already had the write-side bound, attribute-map-merge-fn at 78.6 % of value writes.
(3) THEOREM (CALM, Ameloot et al. 2013). Hypothesis: a fenced merge is order-sensitive, so a deterministic result needs its writes applied in a canonical order, and that needs the knowledge that the write set of the wave is complete. That knowledge is non-monotone, so each DIRECT→fenced hand-off is a quiescence detection with executors parked. A fenced-to-unfenced wake costs another. The number of barriers per S0 run is therefore the number of alternations, not one.
(4) Each alternation also needs the owned slots materialized into the CHAMP for the BSP sub-run, and the fenced writes pushed back. §6.7 places materialization only at boundaries.
findings.direction: Apply D.2's own decision rule now, because the share outside fenced writers is about 11–16 % of fires (counts, not time). That points to the whole-network rule: a network with a fenced cell runs at K = 1 until O-12 (ii) lands. Alternatively, make the fence per facet, with the :type facet of each position as its own fenced component, which P0 §9.6 already said the classification needs. Then unfenced facets of the same position flow DIRECT and only :type writes wait for a canonical-order wave. Change P0-8's question from 'type-cell share' to 'fire-time share outside fenced writers, and alternations per S0 run'. State in §5 and §12.1 that the fence adds one coordination per fenced wave.
findings.falsifier: P0-8's fire-time share outside attribute-map writers is far above the 11–16 % count share. Or E on (make-tagged-merge attribute-map-merge-fn) / attribute-map-merge-fn, with powered :type samples, comes out confirmed. Or the alternation, measured, needs ≤ 1 extra detection per S0 run on the heavy files.

findings.section: D.2 §6.3 'E, made sound' and 'The fence'; §9 Observation 1; §0 row 12; self-critique D2L-4
findings.claim_attacked: "the fence is a monotone map from a merge's property cell to {fenced, free} (contradicted ⇒ fenced)" and "The only non-monotone act left is the detector's predicate"
findings.evidence: THEOREM, from an order argument over SRE's actual lattice. sre-core.rkt:242-260 is a 4-valued diamond: ⊥ = prop-unknown, prop-confirmed, prop-refuted, ⊤ = prop-contradicted, with confirmed ⊔ refuted = ⊤. D.2 mentions only confirmed and contradicted; refuted, the verdict for an undeclared merge whose samples fail (sre-core.rkt:1717), is not mapped. Hypothesis: the fence fails closed, meaning ⊥, refuted and ⊤ are fenced and only confirmed is free. Order {free < fenced}: monotonicity needs f(⊥) ≤ f(confirmed) = free, so ⊥ ↦ free, which is fail-open. Order {fenced < free}: monotonicity needs f(confirmed) = free ≤ f(⊤) = fenced, which is false. So no monotone fail-closed map exists. The existing reader agrees: sre-domain-has-property? 'Returns #t only for prop-confirmed … (capability gating)' (sre-core.rkt:263, 281). It flips #t→#f as confirmed→⊤, a gating read. Also, a live cell's installed merge is replaced at the topology tier, with a fresh closure each time: promote-cell-to-tagged, propagator.rkt:1804-1820, net-cell-reset plus a merge-fns insert. It is called on the attribute-map cell itself from the fork-on-union handler (typing-propagators.rkt:1159, :1211). So 'E once per merge function, registration-time' runs once per promoted cell, and the fence status can change between epochs. Other non-monotone acts inside S0 besides the detector: the alternation's own 'neither has work' tests (§8), and the gate.
findings.direction: Declare the fence what it is: a gating read taken at the topology stratum, once per epoch and fail-closed (fenced unless confirmed), exactly like the partition. Then unify it with ownership. The epoch-indexed, write-once assignment maps each cell to an executor or to the distinguished owner 'fenced' (D2L-2 already says fenced cells have no executor owner). One record carries both placement and fence, and E's verdict cell flows into it at the topology stratum. Give merges an identity as data: a descriptor struct with prop:procedure, built by P1a's combinators, with MergeId = descriptor equality. Then E runs once per descriptor, not once per closure instance. Rewrite §0 row 12 and §9 Observation 1 to list every non-monotone act with its stratum.
findings.falsifier: D.2 states that untested merges are free (an explicit fail-open, defended), that refuted is handled, and that no cell's merge changes after its first S0 epoch. Then the map is monotone as claimed, but the design loses E's fail-closed guarantee.

findings.section: D.2 §6.7 Detection; §9 idle-epoch cell and quiescence-detector
findings.claim_attacked: "idle-epoch : Cell (Vec K Epoch) ; replaces D.1's reset flag" and "declares quiescence of epoch e when Σprod = Σcons and every idle-epoch = e, stable across two scans"
findings.evidence:
MEASUREMENT, an exhaustive interleaving check of a 2-executor model. Command: python3 /Users/avanti/.hermes/profiles/logos-language-designer/cache/scratch/d3/C3/detector_model.py.
Model: per-executor atomic slot reads; drain at the top of the loop with cons += n, as in §6.7; a max-merged idle mark.
With D.2's mark (idle iff idle-epoch = e) a premature declaration is reachable. Shortest witness: E1:IDLE-MARK ; E0:FIRE(sendB) ; E0:IDLE-MARK ; E1:DRAIN(1) ; DET reads ×4 → DECLARE while E1 still has a queued dependent. Once an executor has been idle in epoch e, the max-counter cannot say it became busy again, because the epoch counter removes only the reset across epochs.
With the mark (e, cons_i at the moment of going idle), idle iff mark = (e, cons_i), the check finds no premature state, and the one correct declaration is still reachable.
Power: the checker finds the witness above, and finds the C3-5 witnesses. Under D.2 the false positive is caught only as a spurious 'late-s0-write contradiction (§6.7), so a correct program would fail.
findings.direction: Make idleness information that only grows. Each executor publishes quiet_i = (epoch, cons_i) when its worklist and lanes are empty, joined lexicographically by max. The detector's predicate becomes Σprod = Σcons ∧ ∀i quiet_i = (e, cons_i). An equivalent option is to count the epoch's initial seeds as messages from the scheduler, so the predicate reduces to counters alone. Either way the detector reads only max-counters and the remaining non-monotone part is the comparison itself.
findings.falsifier: D.2 defines cons_i as incremented only after the local cascade a message triggered has drained (not at drain time), and the model check under that definition finds no premature declaration.

findings.claim_attacked: "foreign write → lane[owner][me]; owner joins; dependents enqueue" and "type Lane := Set [CellId Delta]"
findings.direction: Restore the notification as information on the lanes. A lane carries two kinds of element, (cell, delta) and (propagator, wake), both counted in prod and cons. The owner of a changed cell posts a wake into lane[home(p)][owner] for each dependent p homed elsewhere, using the same dependents filter (component paths, worldview). Note that wakes are idempotent (a set), so duplicates cost a fire, never a wrong answer. Add a parity row: a dependent homed on a different executor from its input cell's owner, at K = 2.
findings.falsifier: D.2 specifies that a changed cell's owner fires the dependents itself, so home is the owner of the changed input rather than of the first output, and the counters still cover every cross-executor wake.

findings.section: D.2 §9 scheduler-state cells (ArenaSchedulerNet, :persistent, O-4); §6.6/§6.7 realization; D.1 §14 O-4
findings.claim_attacked: "scheduler-state cells (ArenaSchedulerNet, lifetime :persistent, O-4)": epoch, boundary-epoch, assignment, exec-prod/cons, idle-epoch, lanes, exec-changed, epoch-records as cells; "Every scheduler cell is now monotone"
findings.evidence:
PRECEDENT and code, in the form of a Network Reality Check.
- No ArenaSchedulerNet, scheduler-k or scheduler network exists in production code (grep -rn over racket/prologos excluding tests/benchmarks/tools/compiled: 0 hits). Power: the same files give 49 hits for fuel-cell-id in propagator.rkt.
- No D.2 phase allocates the scheduler network or names a net-new-cell or net-cell-write site for these cells (§12.2's P2/P3 rows).
- §9 Observation 1 says the realization is padded vectors. So prod, cons, idle and lanes have no cell writes: they are scratch.
- The one real scheduler-state cell today is fuel-cell-id (cell 11, propagator.rkt:701). It lives on each computation network and is reset per fork (propagator.rkt:1267). It is written by the scheduler at round entry (Variant A, :3493-3494) or via a local box flushed at boundaries (Variant B, :2690-2712), matching DESIGN_PRINCIPLES.org:922-971: 'The cell is canonical at all observation points; the local-var is scheduler-internal SCRATCH.'
- D.2 instead puts per-run state (epoch, boundary-epoch, assignment, changed sets) in process-wide singletons on a persistent, never-forked network. That is sound only under an unstated invariant that at most one S0 run is live per process, nesting only at boundaries. The S1 NAF handler already quiesces a fork inside the outer run's boundary (process-naf-request, relations.rkt:206, run at :283), and nested quiescence inside a fire is live until row 9 lands (D.2 R-5).
- Map Epoch [...] and Map [Network Epoch] grow monotonically for the life of the process on a :persistent net, with no retirement. P0 §2.2 counts 181 elaborator quiescence calls over 18 files, and the LSP is long-lived.
- At K > 1 nobody is named as the fuel cell's writer. Its merge is min over remaining fuel (tropical-fuel-primitives.rkt:74-75), so two executors that read R and write R−1 lose a decrement.
findings.direction: Write the §9 model in two columns. (a) Real scheduler-state cells, on the run's own network as fuel is, canonical at boundaries, each with its writer and readers named: epoch, boundary-epoch (read by S1, S(−1) and BC-4's completion event), the epoch's assignment-with-fence (C3-3), the fenced set, the epoch record. (b) Scheduler scratch, labelled as such with no lattice claim: prod, cons, quiet marks, lanes, exec-changed, per-executor change counters for fuel. Scratch flushes into (a) at the boundary (Variant B). Process-level state, the pool and K configuration, is what O-4's persistent net is for. Epoch records flow out as a stream to the requester (O-11) instead of accumulating forever. Model the detector as a scheduler algorithm whose output, boundary-epoch, is a cell, not as a propagator.
findings.falsifier: D.2 states and enforces the one-live-S0-run-per-process invariant (nested runs at K = 1 on the calling thread with private counters), gives the persistent maps a retirement rule, and specifies fuel at K > 1. Then singletons are an acceptable realization.

findings.section: D.2 §6.7 Executors; §9 'impl Lattice Nat :as max ; K, epochs, prod/cons counters'; §15 O-11 counter-case; §6.3 D2P-5
findings.claim_attacked: "K is scheduler-k, a cell on the scheduler's network (O-4)", with lattice max
findings.direction: Treat K as a per-run input, not as information that grows. Either read it once at S0-run entry, as O-11's lean (a) does for observation scope, or write it once per run key in a flat lattice. The effective K is then a derived read, min(configured K, the fence rule's verdict for this network). That also makes O-11's two options consistent: both K and observation scope are per-run inputs.
findings.falsifier: D.2 specifies that every K configuration is a separate process and that the D2P-5 rule is realized by a mechanism other than scheduler-k.

findings.section: D.2 §6.6 replay monitor and P2 gate; §14 P2 row
findings.claim_attacked: "re-run S0 from x⁰ₑ under BSP's inner loop and compare the two results cell by cell on the changed cells. Equal on every converted cell is the claim. A difference on a fenced cell is a measurement of order-dependence, not a failure." and the gate "0 differences on converted cells"
findings.evidence:
MEASUREMENT (probe) plus a CONJECTURE about how often contamination occurs.
(1) Compared on whose changed cells? The changed set is DIRECT's per-executor union (§7, D2M-2). A cell that BSP changes and DIRECT does not is never compared, and that is exactly the lost-update or missed-notification class (C3-5's WRONG-FIXPOINT witness). The power row S-8 (X4, two writers, reverse order) changes the cell in both runs, so it cannot show that blind spot.
(2) At K = 1 the fence does nothing ('at K = 1 nothing changes', §6.3), so the fenced attribute-map cell is written in DIRECT order in one run and BSP order in the other. Its merge carries F3(b), which depends on grouping. 84–89 % of fires write that cell (C3-1/C3-2 probe) and nearly every propagator reads it (hub degree 1247 for 657 propagators, census_hub.out). A legitimate order difference on the fenced cell therefore flows into converted cells downstream, and the gate cannot tell that contamination from a scheduler bug.
findings.direction: Compare on changed_DIRECT ∪ changed_BSP. Compute a taint lattice alongside: a converted cell is 'fence-tainted' if some propagator that wrote it read a fenced cell whose two runs differ, or read a tainted cell. That is a monotone OR-closure along the round records' (cell, writers) edges, which O-3 already places in P1/P2. Report clean-cell differences as failures and tainted ones as order-dependence measurements. Add S-8b, a dependent that is never notified (C3-5), which must be flagged.
findings.falsifier: The P2 suite run shows 0 differences on converted cells that read the attribute map, meaning no contamination occurs in practice. And a missed-notification fixture is flagged by the monitor as specified.

findings.claim_attacked: "K = 1 is the same code with one executor." (§5)
findings.evidence:
PRECEDENT, D.2's own text.
- §6.6, P2 at K = 1: 'no ownership, no lane and no detector … Representation is unchanged, the persistent CHAMP network'; writes go 'through net-cell-write's merge directly'.
- §6.7, P3 at K > 1: 'a cell's live value is a slot owned by one executor, published by a single pointer store under release … the CHAMP value form is materialized at boundaries'.
These are two representations with two write paths. The first is CHAMP plus net-cell-write. The second is owned slots, release/acquire, lanes, changed sets and materialization.
So P2's gate (suite at K = 1, replay 0 differences, ≥ 1.4×) validates a path P3 does not run. P3's 'K ∈ {1,4,8,16}' parity row does not say whether its K = 1 is P2's executor or the slot executor with one thread. D.1 §5.1 had stated 'K=1 is the sequential scheduler — not a separate code path'.
findings.direction: Pick one and state it. Option (a): P2 builds the slot representation at K = 1. Lanes then degenerate to K − 1 = 0, the detector to 'worklist empty', and materialization and changed sets run for real, so P2's evidence covers P3's data path. Option (b): retract 'same code', and give P3 a gate row 'slot executor at K = 1 vs P2's executor, replay-equal', so the representation change is tested on its own before parallelism is added.
findings.falsifier: D.2 clarifies that P3's K>1 executor keeps the persistent CHAMP as the live representation, with slots only as a cache that net-cell-write updates. Then the two are the same code.

findings.section: D.2 §6.7 Owned records; §7 epoch records; §10.1 RM-2; §6.6 'the question moves to P3'
findings.claim_attacked: "the CHAMP value form is materialized at boundaries" (§6.7) and RM-2 "cost of materializing x⁰ₑ at K > 1 … decides whether rounds-on-request are offered under DIRECT or only at test time"
findings.direction: Use the changed sets as the delta that flows both ways across a boundary: S0's exec-changed into the CHAMP, and the handlers' and sub-runs' changed cells into the slots. State that x⁰ₑ is the previous boundary's CHAMP pointer. RM-2 then needs no measurement for observation, and rounds-on-request under DIRECT cost one BSP replay from a pointer.
findings.falsifier: The slot form cannot track changes per cell (for example, slots for flat tiers mutated in place without changed-set entries), so a walk is required.

findings.claim_attacked: absence-reading (8) → "an own-output guard that only prevents re-choice → rewrite as a monotone latch on a flat lattice (choose-once ⇒ a ⊤ on a second, different choice); a read of 'unknown as default' → read ⊥ as ⊥; trait/hasmethod bridges that choose on a meta-containing type → declared stratum"
findings.evidence:
PRECEDENT (the Q1 audit's site descriptions) and THEOREM.
- unify-fire (relations.rkt:2132; audit line 352) 'copies only into an absent side; with both sides bound and unequal it does nothing'. That is neither an own-output guard, nor an unknown-as-default read, nor a choosing bridge.
- producer-fire (relations.rkt:2859; audit line 357) 'writes a partial tuple containing scope-cell-bot entries whenever any argument is bound'. That snapshots intermediate states, and none of the three dispositions fits it either.
- THEOREM: a fire into a flat lattice is monotone only if its choice is ⊥ until determined and constant above. A latch whose choice depends on which partial input was seen first gives success under one schedule and ⊤ under another at K > 1. 'choose-once ⇒ ⊤' therefore converts a race into a schedule-dependent contradiction unless the trigger is upward-closed.
findings.direction: Replace the per-site taxonomy with one information-flow rule. A fire writes everything it currently knows, unconditionally; the merge absorbs redundancy; any guard is an upward-closed threshold. For unify-fire, write X ⊔ Y to both sides every time, so P1a row 2's flat lattice gives ⊤ on conflict. For producer-fire, write the tuple into a pointwise-joined cell refined in place, or gate it on 'all arguments bound'. For the bridges, make 'all type arguments ground' the threshold, and keep the declared stratum only for the residual choice on non-ground types (defaulting).
findings.falsifier: The P1b design shows sites 2132 and 2859 fit one of the three listed dispositions without loss, or that every 'choose-once' trigger in the eight sites is upward-closed.

sections_examined: DESIGN_PRINCIPLES.org Statelessness (:700), Orthogonality/Optimization Location Rule (:731-890), Scheduler-State Cells (:892-1014)
